earbuds.motion.title: How silence is made
captions: Noise is a wave of air pressure: high, low, high, low, hitting your ear.
A tiny microphone on the outside hears that wave. The earbud plays the same wave flipped upside down.
Where the wave is high, the flipped one is low. Added together they make an almost flat line: silence.

earbuds.flow.title: Follow the sound
captions: The crowd's noise reaches the outside microphone first.
A chip flips the wave, faster than the sound can travel into your ear.
The speaker plays the flipped wave and it meets the noise inside your ear: they cancel.
Your music is left untouched, so you hear it clearly over the quiet.

earbuds.number.title: The number
captions: Good earbuds can make a low hum, like an engine, sound 10 to 30 times quieter.
Low sounds are long, slow waves, easy to match. Voices and clicks are short and fast, so some get through.
That is why a plane's drone disappears but a person talking next to you does not.
